thread:
lee-recruiter: Heads-up: Sunita (start 2026-11-02) has an H1B extension pending and needs to travel internationally for a family emergency next week. She asked whether we should delay start or proceed and how benefits/tax/visa paperwork are impacted. cc @marta-peopleops @robert-hiringmgr
marta-peopleops: Oof. Short: travel during H1B adjudication is risky. For benefits, we can provisionally enroll dependents if docs/receipts exist, but I9 / final eligibility depends on physical presence and docs. Do we have travel dates?
sunita-newhire: Travel 2026-10-20 to 2026-10-27. USCIS receipt for H1 extension filed 3 weeks ago (receipt # ends 3002). I can delay start if needed but hope we can keep 11/2. Also spouse on H4 not traveling. Uploaded receipts + travel itinerary to drive: https://drive.company/boxed/sunita/imm
imm-legal: Legal note: leaving the US while an H1B extension is pending may be treated as abandoning the extension filing depending on consulate processing. If Sunita has valid H1 visa stamp and passport, reentry possible but risky. Recommend consult with immigration attorney and avoid travel if possible. Also, for I-9: physical presence for Section 2 is required unless we use alternative remote procedures.
robert-hiringmgr: From team: we prefer she join on schedule if safe. Can we do remote onboarding from abroad for a week? Are there payroll/tax implications?
travel-ops: Travel FYI: if she exits, make sure she carries original H1 approval notice (if any), receipt, and employer letter. We can prepare an employer letter quickly.
benefits-bot: Benefits note: Provisional enrollments for dependents require documentation. Medical coverage effective date can be start date if enrollment submitted timely; vendor may require SSN later. If Sunita is not physically present for first week, vendor still accepts enrollments as long as HRIS has the record. Premiums billed as usual.
marta-peopleops: Operational plan: 1) Hold off on in-person I-9 until she's back OR do a WorkBright remote verification (we use "receipt" policy for extensions) 2) Provision equipment and remote access for first week but restrict privileged access until final docs; 3) Open travel/legal check.
imm-legal: We'll set up a quick consult. Also note: if H1 extension is RFE-prone, offshore travel might complicate processes. Advise delay if travel non-essential. If travel unavoidable, document employer letter and wage verification for re-entry.
sunita-newhire: Thank you. I do have a valid H1 visa stamp that expires 2027. I can carry the employer letter. If I do remote onboarding, can payroll and benefits still start 11/2?
marta-peopleops: Yes payroll can start 11/2. We'll enroll benefits and set I-9 as "remote receipt" pending physical docs; WorkBright session required. Payroll will deduct premiums; vendor reconciles if SSN/EAD not present.
robert-hiringmgr: Sounds good. Approve remote-first-week and limited permissions. We want Sunita onboarded ASAP.
travel-ops: I'll prep the employer letter and send to Sunita today. Also recommend she carries copies of paystubs/offer letter when re-entering.
imm-legal: We'll schedule a 20-min call to advise on re-entry risk. Also set a 30-day follow-up to collect any additional docs.
benefits-bot: Noted: please upload travel docs + receipt to the employee folder and tag benefits@redwood. Vendor case will be opened if needed.
sunita-newhire: Uploaded employer letter request and itinerary. Thank you all. If counsel says high risk I'll postpone travel.
marta-peopleops: I'll open WorkBright remote I-9 slot for 10/25 and flag "pending H1 extension". If she can't make it we will do Section 2 verification in person on return.
robert-hiringmgr: Thanks team. Keep me posted.
lee-recruiter: I'll message Sunita and confirm the plan. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
